`task desktop:dev` runs reflex-desktop `dev`, which scaffolds `tauri-dev/src-tauri/` (remote backend) and only writes the DesktopPlugin options into its tauri.conf.json. The vibrancy settings copied from vermoegen (`windowEffects` liquidGlassRegular+sidebar, Overlay title bar, trafficLightPosition 16/26, `macOSPrivateApi`, Cargo feature `macos-private-api`) are hand edits and must exist in both `tauri/` and `tauri-dev/`. Hand edits survive `_configure`.

**Why:** without them the dev window is `transparent: true` with no material, so the desktop behind shows through (2026-10-15).
**How to apply:** when the window looks see-through or differs between dev and run, diff the two tauri.conf.json files; if `tauri-dev/` is deleted and re-scaffolded, re-add the settings.

I've changed the desktop build so the header makes room for the window buttons when the sidebar is collapsed. I haven't looked at the result in the window yet. Restart `task desktop:dev` to see it, because the attribute is set at compile time.

**Cause:** the CSS already had an 84px left padding for the toolbar in this case. It only applies when the `data-native` attribute is on `<html>`, and that attribute was never set in the dev window. The window loads a remote URL, so the Tauri globals aren't there yet when the head script runs, and the check silently failed.

**Fix:** in [theme.py](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/theme.py), desktop builds (`is_desktop()`) now set `data-native` unconditionally. The Tauri-global check stays for every other build, so the web version is unchanged, as you wanted.

content.text:
I've fixed the selector, so the header should now sit to the right of the window buttons when the sidebar is collapsed. I haven't seen it in the desktop window. Reload `task desktop:dev` to check it. The commons tests pass (226) and ruff is clean on the two files I changed.

The 84px padding for the traffic lights never applied, because the selector in [shell.py:78](components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/components/shell.py#L78) was `html[data-native]html[data-sidebar-collapsed] .aq-toolbar`. That is two `html` selectors with nothing between them, so it matched nothing. It is now `html[data-native][data-sidebar-collapsed] .aq-toolbar`, which is only active in the desktop window, so the web version is unchanged. The test in [test_shell.py:90](components/alloq-commons/tests/test_shell.py#L90) had the broken selector hard-coded, so I updated it too.

My earlier `theme.py` change was a wrong guess, since `data-native` was already being set, and I've reverted it.
